title: Quant telemetry fusion and deployment guardrail for hybrid-precision variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We onboarded several hybrid-precision variants (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8) but lack a consolidated telemetry signal that correlates latency/throughput regressions with subtle output-quality drift. This makes automated canaries noisy and forces manual rollbacks or overly conservative pinning.

Goal: Build a telemetry-fusion guardrail that ingests perf metrics (latency P50/P95, token/sec, GPU utilization), model-side signals (kv-cache hit/miss patterns, mem transfers), and quality proxies (eval-set BLEU/EM-like scores, semantic embedding drift, token distribution KL) to produce a single "canary health score." Use the score to gate staging->production rollouts, enable automatic short-term pinning to a stable variant, and emit clear actionables for engineers and PMs.

Scope:
- Define fused telemetry schema and score computation.
- Add ingestion hooks to the existing runtime telemetry pipeline.
- Create a lightweight canary orchestrator that samples live traffic per-route and computes rolling health scores.
- Define gating thresholds and rollback policies for automated pin/unpin.
- Surface signals in a console dashboard and runtime alerting.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary health score computed every 1 minute for each canary cohort.
- Score thresholds documented and validated on 3 internal workloads.
- Automated short-term pin triggers when health score < 0.75 for 3 consecutive minutes; create audit entry + incident ticket.
- Dashboard card + GitHub PR link visible in rollout UI.

Non-goals: full retraining or human-labeled accuracy audits (we rely on proxy evals and customer-facing regression alerts).
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha: Initial spike completed. Prototype for fused schema (perf+quality) in notebook; see /drive/quant-telemetry/prototype. Next: formalize schema and map to runtime events.

2026-02-24 - Marcus: POC ingestion plugin landed on branch feat/quant-telemetry-ingest (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2483). It emits perf and kv-cache metrics to the metrics bus with a canary tag.

2026-03-02 - SRE (Jordan Lee): Memory accounting change in runtime caused 4% higher mem copies in early canary; flagged in canary logs. We added a short-term mitigation to throttle prefetching during canary runs. See incident notes: /drive/incidents/2026-03-02-kv-prefetch.md.

2026-03-04 - Data Sci (Priya Nair): Added embedding drift proxy (cosine drop on a fixed prompt set) and a token-distribution KL metric. Initial correlation analysis across 12 quant variants shows KL > 0.06 often aligns with small BLEU drops.

2026-03-07 - Marcus: Integrated score computation service with rollout engine. Default weights: latency(0.45), throughput(0.2), embedding-drift(0.25), kl-token-dist(0.1). We will tune weights after the internal A/B run.

2026-03-09 - PM (Daniel Ruiz): Agreed on automation policy: health < 0.75 triggers temporary pin for 30 minutes and notify owners; health < 0.6 triggers immediate rollback to previous variant and PagerDuty. Added to release notes for runtime-1.20.

2026-03-10 - Marcus: Completed canary A/B run on three internal services (chat-demo, rerank, summarizer). Results: average health score drop of 0.12 for AWQ variant on long-context workload driven by P95 latency spike (+18%) and embedding drift (0.08). We pinned AWQ for chat-demo and opened ENG-121009 to investigate kernel scheduling for long sequences.
next_steps: Tune score weights with 6 additional production-like workloads (target completion 2026-03-20). Drive a follow-up ENG ticket for kernel optimization if AWQ long-context regressions persist (ENG-121009). Add per-customer sensitivity flags to lower automation aggressiveness for high-risk customers.
